headline: Google Keep productivity system uses 3 layers for organization
summary: A tech journalist shares his custom system for managing notes, ideas, and tasks using only Google Keep, bypassing complex productivity apps.
details: Dhruv Bhutani, an experienced tech journalist, has developed a unique productivity system entirely within Google Keep. He found that many other productivity apps are overly complex, leading him to rely on Keep's simplicity for managing everything from article ideas to personal tasks.

The core of his system involves using a blank note as the starting point, then layering labels, pins, and checklists to organize information. Bhutani emphasizes the importance of capturing ideas immediately, creating a fresh note for any inspiration that strikes, whether it's a story angle or a personal reminder.

Labels are used to create broad categories, such as 'work' or 'personal tasks,' helping to group related notes. This allows for efficient management of diverse information streams, like keeping all work-related notes separate from personal projects.

Within these categories, Bhutani leverages keywords and Keep's powerful search function to find specific information. The search can even pull text from images, a feature he uses for notes on books by taking photos of pages he wants to remember.

The final organizational layer involves pinned notes. These are reserved for items actively being worked on, such as a grocery list or an ongoing project. Once completed, the note is unpinned and returned to its place in the general note collection.

This three-layer system—labels for broad categories, search for specific details, and pinned notes for active tasks—allows for efficient organization without the complexity of apps like Notion. Bhutani highlights that setting up this system requires minimal effort, often just a few keystrokes.

headline_marked: Withings BodyScan 2: [[ECG and AI health assistant]] for $600
headline: Withings BodyScan 2: ECG and AI health assistant for $600
summary: The $600 smart scale offers daily scans and a weekly 90-second 'longevity scan' that includes a full ECG and blood oxygen measurement.
details: The Withings BodyScan 2 smart scale is priced at $600 and offers advanced health tracking features, including a full electrocardiogram (ECG) and blood oxygen measurements.
Daily scans take about 30 seconds and provide metrics like weight, body composition estimates, basal metabolic rate, vascular age, and pulse wave velocity.
The more intensive 90-second 'longevity scan,' recommended weekly, adds blood oxygen level (SpO2) and a six-lead ECG capable of detecting atrial fibrillation.
All data syncs to the Withings mobile app, which requires a $10/month or $100/year subscription to Withings+ to unlock its full potential.
Withings+ features an AI health assistant that analyzes your data, offering insights into vascular and heart age, and various health scores.
The subscription model and the need for additional Withings products to track nutrition and steps are noted as potential drawbacks.
